successors.note: Cliopatria's Haryanka row reaches the Mallas' latitude only in -450 (bbox to 27.80N); the Malla page has the annexation by 468 BCE, so the land is Magadha's from -468 here.

capitals.name: Kusinārā (Kushinagar, village of Kāsiā)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Kusinārā, Pāvā': the Mallas were two republics, Kusinārā ('identified with the modern village of Kāsiā in Kushinagar') and Pāvā ('now known as Fazilnagar'), divided by the Hiraññavatī river. Kusinārā is the one capital dot; neither name is in the gazetteer.

keyframe_review.note: 5,486 km2 disc (centroid 84.15E 26.63N), about 75 km east of Gorakhpur, for -600..-481. The page says 'The Mallas lived in the region now covered by the Kushinagar district', 'their neighbours to the east across the Sadānirā river were the Licchavikas' and 'The territory of the Mallas was a tract of land between the Vaidehas and the Kauśalyas'; it gives no area. A core of two republics of that size is the right order, so the disc stands.

correction.text: the shape unchanged but only for -480..-469: by 468 BCE Magadha had 'annex[ed] its territories' of the Vajjika League, to which both Malla republics belonged

keyframe_review.note: Years only: the disc is right but Cliopatria keeps it 17 years too long (to -451). The page has Ajatashatru 'declared war on the Vajjika League in 484 BCE', Magadha able 'to finally defeat the Vajjika League by 468 BCE and annex its territories', and 'Both Malla republics nevertheless became members of the Licchavi-led Vajjika League' and 'The Mallas also became part of Ajatashatru's Māgadhī empire'. The shape therefore holds -480..-469, not to -451. The page's infobox 'Disestablished: c. 4th century BCE' is the end of the republics inside the empire ('they stopped existing as a republican tribe when the Maurya dynasty ruled Magadha or shortly after'), not of Malla independence.

region.text: the Mallas' land: 'the region now covered by the Kushinagar district', 'a tract of land between the Vaidehas and the Kauśalyas', Kusinārā and Pāvā

ledger.note: c. 600 BCE: the Mallas of Kusinārā and Pāvā stand as one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas on the Kushinagar country. Infobox 'Established: c. 7th century BCE', 'Aristocratic Republic'; the Mahajanapadas page has the Mallakas 'originally' a monarchy that 'later ... switched to one of Samgha (republican union)'. -600 is Cliopatria's start, so the year is a bridge.

region.text: the Mallas' land: 'the region now covered by the Kushinagar district', 'a tract of land between the Vaidehas and the Kauśalyas', Kusinārā and Pāvā

ledger.note: 468 BCE: Magadha annexes the Vajjika League and the Mallas with it. 'he declared war on the Vajjika League in 484 BCE'; Magadha was able 'to finally defeat the Vajjika League by 468 BCE and annex its territories'; 'The Mallas also became part of Ajatashatru's Māgadhī empire.' The page does not date the Mallas' fall itself, so the League's year is read for them; the Mahajanapadas page has them annexed 'not long after Buddha's death'. Cliopatria ends the row in -451.

wars.name: Magadhan conquest of the Vajjika League
wars.outcome: Ajatashatru 'declared war on the Vajjika League in 484 BCE' and Magadha 'finally defeat[ed] the Vajjika League by 468 BCE and annex[ed] its territories'; the Mallas, members of the League, became part of his empire.
wars.note: No battle or front is named in Malla land, so no contested zone is drawn; the annexation is the dissolve event. Relations before the war: the Mallas 'held friendly relations with the Licchavikas, the Vaidehas, and the Nāyikas' and Magadha's relations with the Licchavikas 'were initially good'. The Haryanka page (Ajatashatru 493-462) fits the 484-468 span.

certainty.note: The Sadānirā (Gandak) to the east and the Hiraññavatī between the two republics are the only lines the page gives; the Kosala and Videha frontiers are approximate.

notes: The end is moved from Cliopatria's -451 to -468 because the Malla page dates the annexation of the Vajjika League 'by 468 BCE' and has the Mallas, members of the League, join Ajatashatru's empire (confidence 2: the page does not date the Mallas separately). The page's infobox end 'c. 4th century BCE' and 'they stopped existing as a republican tribe when the Maurya dynasty ruled Magadha or shortly after' are the end of the republics inside Magadha, not of independence. The Vajji dossier (janapada-of-vajji, Cliopatria -600..-481) and the Haryanka dossier should carry the League's side; the page's chronology (Ajatashatru's war 484-468) differs from the Magadha page's (Sarao: Ajatashatru c. 405-373). Undated and left out of the ledger: Mallakas who 'helped Pasenadi's son Viḍūḍabha usurp the throne of Kosala' (Kosala page), the murder of Bandhula by Pasenadi. The Mallas' share in the Buddha's relics (Kusinārā, Pāvā) has no territorial effect. Pages: Malla and the shared Mahajanapadas page. Gazetteer lacks: Kushinagar/Kusinara (place, 26.74N 83.89E, village of Kasia) and Pava (Fazilnagar), used only in the capital entry.
